title: Errands
eyebrow: 11 jobs a person can do and this archive cannot
dek: Every one of these needs a login, a card, an identity check or a human being in a reading room. They are drafted, costed and ordered by what they would settle.
lead: An archive that can only use what is free and unauthenticated will stop at a particular place, and this one has stopped there. What follows is the queue past that point. Each entry says what the source is, what it would settle, and roughly what it costs — so that anyone who wants to help can pick one up without asking what to do.

rows.what: GRO birth certificate — Miriam Wakefield, Jun quarter 1840, Bristol, vol 11 page 183
rows.where: General Register Office, gro.gov.uk (an account, no visit)
rows.settles: It names her mother WITH HER MAIDEN SURNAME. Five Queensland death registrations now say Saniger in four spellings, so the name itself is settled — but not one English record has ever confirmed it, and the 1841 census says Hannah was born OUTSIDE Gloucestershire, which is why no Gloucestershire register will ever find her. This certificate is the only document identified that attacks the question from the English end.
rows.why: THE CHEAPEST DECISIVE DOCUMENT ON THIS SITE

rows.what: Run the NSW BDM historical index for the D'Arcys
rows.cost: free, ten minutes, but behind a bot check
rows.settles: The entire D'Arcy side were New South Welshmen. George Pitt D'Arcy died at Parramatta in 1849, George Lindsay was born there in 1829, Frederick Robert and Charlotte both crossed. NSW death registrations name the parents of the deceased — which is how Queensland's index settled the Saniger name five times over. This is the largest free index this archive has never searched, and it is shut to an automated browser.

rows.what: PROB 11/1728/64 — the will of Major-General Robert D'Arcy
rows.settles: His parentage is the largest open question on this site and no record of his life names a father. A will names family. Found 9 September 2026 and still unordered.

rows.what: Enquiry to the Royal Engineers Museum, Chatham
rows.settles: Robert D'Arcy's parentage, from the records of the Corps he served for fifty-one years and the town he died in.
rows.why: The best chance of closing the question the archive was built around

rows.where: Queensland Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages
rows.settles: Three causes of death, and three sets of parents named in a civil record rather than a tree. Registration numbers already identified.
rows.why: Turns three dotted pedigree edges solid

rows.settles: Robert D'Arcy, 1827, and Constantine D'Arcy, 1805. A burial register can give an age, an abode and sometimes a relationship.
rows.why: The likeliest of all of these to succeed

rows.what: Where Arthur Hartley Sneyd is commemorated
rows.settles: The archive says Villers-Bretonneux from the B.2090A's “Not yet to hand”. CWGC would confirm it outright. Bot-blocked here, twice.
rows.why: Free, quick, and this archive simply cannot reach it

rows.settles: The Ayrshire Murdochs are a quarter of the tested descendant and the archive has 25 of 52 ancestor slots filled. The DNA points straight at this gap.
rows.why: The branch the archive has most neglected

rows.what: Richard Atkinson and Anne, of Limerick
rows.settles: Anything at all. The Atkinsons are five generations deep and stop dead at the emigrant.

Arthur Hartley Sneyd's 1916 intestacy; William Hartley Sneyd's 1873 insolvency — a wholly new fact; four wills, one of which may be the gaol governor's; two police staff files that are probably his sons.
rows.why: All nine identified to series and file number

rows.what: Which Ordnance series could carry a Royal Engineers commission of 1776
rows.settles: WO 47 has been identified along with the reason nobody has found him in it. A archivist could say in a sentence whether it is worth a day.

ydna.what: A Y-DNA test from a male D'Arcy
ydna.settles: The Y chromosome descends father to son essentially unchanged. A male-line D'Arcy's would place this family against every other tested D'Arcy in the world — the most direct attack anyone can make on Robert D'Arcy's parentage, and it beats every archive visit on this page.
ydna.note: The descendant who has tested is female and has no Y chromosome. Her brothers do.

close: Several of these will come back empty. That is a result, and it belongs on the search register rather than in a drawer — so that the next person does not repeat it.
